tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (job fails, times out, scores only part of input, whether to use batch vs real-time endpoint) rather than internal implementation, explicitly covers trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name technical terms ('even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType, MaxPayloadInMB...'), and while lengthy, it remains a single cohesive paragraph focused on scope rather than padding.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when the user asks whether a large periodic scoring run should use batch transform or a real-time endpoint, or whether scored output is protected, even if they do not mention JSON Lines, SplitType, MaxPayloadInMB, ModelClientConfig, JoinSource, MaxConcurrentTransforms or KMS keys by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body skips explaining general concepts (what batch transform is, what S3 is) and jumps straight into domain-specific routing, check IDs, severities, and known pitfalls specific to SageMaker batch transform. Sections are terse tables and bullet lists rather than verbose prose.
tests.evidence: Activate this skill when the user: - Reports a transform job that Failed — an input format or ContentType mismatch...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (full check catalog, detection rules, remediations, API quirks) is explicitly deferred to references/ files; the body only contains a compact index table and router, not the full detail.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition for when to load it, not just a generic 'see' pointer.
tests.evidence: load it before assigning any check-id or severity; load it whenever the user names a specific error or symptom; load it before interpreting any empty metric or a Completed status

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All references use relative paths from the skill root in the format references/<filename>.md.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-critical parts (guardrails, check-id assignment, validation gate) are prescriptive with explicit non-negotiable rules, while flexible parts (how to diagnose a given symptom, the review procedure) explain reasoning and intent rather than dictating rigid steps.
tests.evidence: 1. Read-only. Never call a transform mutation... Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal choices; it routes deterministically by symptom to a single API/approach in the Router table.
tests.evidence: Does not apply — the skill does not present interchangeable tool options; evaluation based on absence of any multi-option listing.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (symptom matching, router, check catalog, validation gate) applicable to any batch transform job, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section documenting concrete, non-obvious pitfalls (e.g., Completed != fully scored, absent CloudWatch datapoints != zero) that the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: "The job is Completed, so every record was scored." Completed means the job ran to the end. The output .out object count can be short of the input record count...

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its findings, check-ids, severities, and evidence before presenting, which is genuine self-validation rather than procedural work.
tests.evidence: A wrong or unsupported finding is worse than a slow one. Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
